tagline: Read YouTube Reporting/Analytics metadata and safely plan documented job/group mutations.

source_cli.name: YouTube Analytics and Reporting APIs
source_cli.reference: Google Discovery: YouTube Analytics API v2 revision 20260803 and YouTube Reporting API v1 revision 20260803

global_flags.name: credential
global_flags.summary: Credential name to use for the YouTube request.

global_flags.name: connection
global_flags.summary: Credential name alias used only when --credential is omitted; does not resolve pm connections.

global_flags.name: config
global_flags.summary: Connector config override as key=value; never pass secret values here.

global_flags.name: limit
global_flags.summary: Maximum records to emit from stream commands.

global_flags.name: preview
global_flags.summary: Preview a reverse-ETL write command without making a network mutation.

global_flags.name: approval-token-stdin
global_flags.summary: Read the approval token as one bounded line from standard input.

global_flags.name: confirm
global_flags.summary: Typed confirmation challenge for destructive reverse-ETL writes.

commands.summary: Read YouTube Reporting jobs through the declared ETL stream.

flags.name: include-system-managed
flags.summary: Include system-managed reporting jobs.

commands.summary: Read one YouTube Reporting job by configured job_id.
commands.notes: Pass --config job_id=<job id>; ETL command flags intentionally map only to query parameters, not connector config path variables.
examples: pm youtube-analytics jobs get --credential youtube-prod --config job_id=job_fixture_1 --json

commands.summary: Plan creation of a YouTube Reporting job.

flags.name: report-type-id
flags.summary: ReportType id the job should generate.

flags.name: name
flags.summary: Reporting job display name required by the provider.

commands.risk: Creates a scheduled YouTube Reporting job; requires reverse ETL plan, preview, explicit approval, then execute.
commands.approval: Plan first, inspect preview output, then run only with the generated approval token.
examples: pm youtube-analytics jobs create --credential youtube-prod --report-type-id channel_basic_a3 --name 'Daily channel basics' --preview --json

commands.summary: Plan deletion of a YouTube Reporting job with typed destructive confirmation.

flags.name: job-id
flags.summary: Reporting job ID to delete.

commands.risk: Destructive job deletion stops future report generation; redacts job_id from previews/errors; requires reverse ETL plan, preview, explicit approval, and --confirm destructive before execute.
commands.approval: Plan first, inspect preview output, then run only with the generated approval token and typed --confirm destructive challenge.
examples: pm youtube-analytics jobs delete --credential youtube-prod --job-id job_fixture_delete --preview --json

commands.summary: Read YouTube Reporting report types through the declared ETL stream.

flags.name: include-system-managed
flags.summary: Include system-managed report types.

commands.summary: Read generated report metadata for the configured YouTube Reporting job.

flags.name: created-after
flags.summary: createdAfter filter for reports.list.

flags.name: start-time-at-or-after
flags.summary: startTimeAtOrAfter filter for reports.list.

flags.name: start-time-before
flags.summary: startTimeBefore filter for reports.list.

commands.notes: Pass --config job_id=<job id>; downloaded report bytes are intentionally not emitted by this JSON metadata stream.
examples: pm youtube-analytics reports list --credential youtube-prod --config job_id=job_fixture_1 --limit 25 --json

commands.summary: Read one generated report metadata resource for the configured job_id/report_id.
commands.notes: Pass --config job_id=<job id> --config report_id=<report id>; use reports download with the documented resourceName to fetch report bytes.
examples: pm youtube-analytics reports get --credential youtube-prod --config job_id=job_fixture_1 --config report_id=report_fixture_1 --json

commands.summary: Documented YouTube Analytics reports.query provider query operation planned for issue #2985.
commands.notes: Planned solely until typed provider-query foundation issue #2985 supports bounded provider-owned query fields without raw query escape hatches.

commands.summary: Download generated YouTube Reporting report bytes to an explicit local destination.

flags.name: resource-name
flags.summary: Provider resourceName identifying the generated report; may contain safe path segments.

commands.notes: The required --resource-name maps to the provider resourceName. Runtime download flags require --dest-root; --file-name is optional. The executor refuses path traversal, overwrites, archive extraction, and payloads over 100 MiB, and emits only file metadata with a SHA-256 receipt.

commands.summary: Read YouTube Analytics groups through the declared ETL stream.

flags.name: mine
flags.summary: Required closed groups.list selector; only the provider-valid mine=true mode is supported.

examples: pm youtube-analytics groups list --credential youtube-prod --mine true --limit 25 --json

commands.summary: Plan creation of a YouTube Analytics group.

flags.name: title
flags.summary: Group title.

flags.name: item-type
flags.summary: Provider resource type the group will contain.

commands.risk: Creates a YouTube Analytics group; requires reverse ETL plan, preview, explicit approval, then execute.
commands.approval: Plan first, inspect preview output, then run only with the generated approval token.
examples: pm youtube-analytics groups create --credential youtube-prod --title 'Owned fixture group' --item-type youtube#video --preview --json

commands.summary: Plan update of a YouTube Analytics group's title.

flags.name: id
flags.summary: YouTube Analytics group id to update.

flags.name: title
flags.summary: Replacement group title.

commands.risk: Mutates YouTube Analytics group metadata; redacts group id from write errors; requires reverse ETL plan, preview, explicit approval, then execute.
commands.approval: Plan first, inspect preview output, then run only with the generated approval token.
examples: pm youtube-analytics groups update --credential youtube-prod --id group_fixture_1 --title 'Renamed fixture group' --preview --json

commands.summary: Plan deletion of a YouTube Analytics group with typed destructive confirmation.

flags.name: id
flags.summary: YouTube Analytics group id to delete.

commands.risk: Destructive group deletion; redacts group id from previews/errors; requires reverse ETL plan, preview, explicit approval, and --confirm destructive before execute.
commands.approval: Plan first, inspect preview output, then run only with the generated approval token and typed --confirm destructive challenge.
examples: pm youtube-analytics groups delete --credential youtube-prod --id group_fixture_delete --preview --json

commands.summary: Read items in a YouTube Analytics group through the declared ETL stream.

flags.name: group-id
flags.summary: Group ID for the required groupItems.list groupId query value.

examples: pm youtube-analytics group-items list --credential youtube-prod --group-id group_fixture_1 --limit 100 --json

commands.summary: Plan adding a channel, playlist, video, or asset to a YouTube Analytics group.

flags.name: group-id
flags.summary: Group ID to add the resource to.

flags.name: resource-kind
flags.summary: Optional provider resource kind being added.

flags.name: resource-id
flags.summary: Resource ID being added.

commands.risk: Adds an item to a YouTube Analytics group; redacts group/resource identifiers from write errors; requires reverse ETL plan, preview, explicit approval, then execute.
commands.approval: Plan first, inspect preview output, then run only with the generated approval token.
examples: pm youtube-analytics group-items create --credential youtube-prod --group-id group_fixture_1 --resource-kind youtube#video --resource-id video_fixture_1 --preview --json

commands.summary: Plan removal of an item from a YouTube Analytics group with typed destructive confirmation.

flags.name: id
flags.summary: Group item id to remove.

commands.risk: Destructive removal of a group item; redacts group-item id from previews/errors; requires reverse ETL plan, preview, explicit approval, and --confirm destructive before execute.
commands.approval: Plan first, inspect preview output, then run only with the generated approval token and typed --confirm destructive challenge.
examples: pm youtube-analytics group-items delete --credential youtube-prod --id group_item_fixture_delete --preview --json

help_topics.name: binary-downloads
help_topics.summary: Generated report metadata includes download_url; use reports download with the documented resourceName and an explicit destination root to fetch report bytes safely.

help_topics.name: content-owner-writes
help_topics.summary: Read streams support onBehalfOfContentOwner from content_owner_id; declarative write actions omit that optional query until write-action query templates are available.

help_topics.name: destructive-confirmation
help_topics.summary: YouTube Reporting job deletes and YouTube Analytics group/group-item deletes require reverse ETL plan, preview, explicit approval, and typed destructive confirmation.
